chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqub said:

I sent a basket to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) containing Narbaj, so he ate from it and said: 'Withhold the remainder of it for me.' It was brought to him twice or three times. Then the slave poured water into it and brought it to him, so he said to him: 'Woe be unto you! You have spoiled it for me.'

key_terms.نَارْبَاجُ: Narbaj, a type of preserved fruit or food item mentioned in Shia hadith literature.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or etiquette regarding the consumption of Narbaj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s attention to sensory details in food preparation, specifically regarding 'Narbaj' (likely a preserved fruit or sweetmeat), where premature hydration ruined its texture or flavor. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and mindfulness in daily acts, transforming mundane culinary practices into opportunities for spiritual refinement and appreciation of Allah’s blessings. The rebuke highlights that proper timing and method are essential to preserving the integrity of sustenance, reflecting a broader Islamic principle of avoiding waste and maximizing benefit.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I sent a basket to Abu Abdullahasws and in it was Narbaja. So heasws ate from it and said: ‘Withhold the remainder of it for me, so bring it to me twice or three (times)’. Then the slave put water in it, and came up with it. So heasws said to him: ‘Woe be unto you! You have spoilt it for me’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Walid has narrated from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who has said the following: “

I once sent for abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a cooking pot with al-Nar Bajah in it (broth made of pomegranate). He (the Imam) ate from it and told to save the rest for him to have it twice or three times. The slave then added water in it and brought it to him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Fie upon you. You have destroyed it.’”
